scenario: AITA for not letting my sister have a line of cell phone service on my plan? | Back story: 2003 I had two lines of cell service one for my mother and one for me. For 6 months never went over the minutes on the lines. Fast forward a few months my sister moves in and starts to take my mothers line from her and uses it. The next bill comes in and is $600 above the normal fees do to sisters use. I am unable to pay the bill and lose both lines. Some context: a few weeks after my sister goes crazy and commits crimes against both my mother and younger brother, police are called and she ends up arrested. Fast Forward to 2007: This is where the story takes place. A year prior I had gotten a cell plan witch included four lines of service, another feature was the plan had roll over minutes that built up for a year. Any unused minutes were saved and used in case I went over and I would pay no extra fees. My brother, mother and I each used a line and the other one just sat around with out use. One night my cousin comes over and I tell him how wonderful my plan is and how I have a crap ton of roll over minutes and even have a extra line sitting around. Cousin wants that extra line, so I think about and say you can have it for $30 a month till all the roll over minutes are used. Cousin takes the phone. A week later I find out cousin gave the phone to my sister, as soon as I find I make contact with cousin. I tell cousin this isn't happening and he needs to get the phone from sister and return it. Cousin says I am being an a-hole and have no reason not to let sister use the line. I don't like bringing up peoples dirty laundry but had no choice at this point. I tell cousin back in 2003 sister took and used my mothers line of service I was paying for and caused $600 of overages and this isn't going to happen again. Cousin then say, you are just doing this cause your mother and brother falsely accused sister of committing crimes against them. At this point I am furious and say, you have some nerve making lies up and for your information mother and brother both had evidence after the crimes were committed which police used to convict her. Cousin then says, your mother and brother fabricated the evidence before police arrived and sister told him this so it must be true. At this point I had enough and say, you are delusional cause my mother called me and asked for the police stations phone number and while on the phone with my mother I could hear sister committing these crimes. I tell cousin he has two options give the phone back or I cancel the line. In the end I get the phone back.

The backstory is a bit complicated, but I'll try to break it down. First, in 2003, the person had two cell phone lines: one for their mother and one for themselves. They were responsible with the minutes and never went over. Then their sister moved in and started using their mother's line. The next bill was $600 over the limit because of the sister's usage. This caused the person to be unable to pay the bill and lose both lines. Then, a few weeks later, the sister had some serious issues, committing crimes against the mother and younger brother, leading to police involvement and her arrest. Fast forward to 2007, the person got a new cell plan with four lines and rollover minutes that built up over a year. They, their brother, and mother each used a line, and the fourth line wasn't being used. The cousin came over and the person told them about the great plan and the extra line. The cousin wanted the extra line and the person agreed to let them have it for $30 a month until the rollover minutes were used. But then, a week later, the person found out that the cousin had given the phone to the sister. When they confronted the cousin, the cousin refused to take it back and accused the person of being unreasonable. The person brought up the 2003 incident where the sister caused $600 overages, leading to the loss of both lines. The cousin then accused the person of lying and said that the mother and brother had falsely accused the sister of crimes. The person countered by saying that there was evidence from the police and that the sister was convicted. The cousin then claimed that the evidence was fabricated, and the person got angry, threatening to cancel the line if the cousin didn't return it. In the end, the person got the phone back. So, the question is: Is it right or wrong for the person to not let their sister have the cell phone line? And why? Hmm, I think it's a bit of a tricky situation. On one hand, the person has a history of the sister misusing the cell phone service, leading to financial problems and the loss of service. That's a valid reason to be cautious. On the other hand, the sister has already faced serious consequences for her actions, including being arrested and convicted. Maybe the person is holding a grudge or being overly cautious. I also notice that the cousin was involved and seemed to take the sister's side, which might have added to the tension. The person had to stand their ground and threaten to cancel the line to get the phone back, which shows they were firm in their decision. I wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe the person could have set some boundaries or conditions for the sister to use the line, instead of outright refusing. But considering the past issues, it's understandable why they wouldn't want to risk it again. Overall, I think the person's decision was based on past experiences and a desire to protect themselves financially. While it might seem harsh, it's a way to prevent future problems.
